pong_binary_search_interception.name: Pong — Binary Search Interception
pong_binary_search_interception.rules: Predict the frame at which the ball crosses the paddle's x-line by binary searching on the monotonic predicate ballX(frame) >= paddleX (or <= for a leftward ball), then recover the y-coordinate by unfolding wall bounces.

tetris_best_fit.name: Tetris — Best-Fit Memory Allocation
tetris_best_fit.rules: Place incoming memory blocks using Best-Fit allocation to minimize fragmentation.

dice_roll_simulator_amortized_rerender.name: Dice-Roll-Simulator — Amortized Analysis of Full-List Re-rendering
dice_roll_simulator_amortized_rerender.rules: This simulation models the rendering cost of updating a list UI naively by re-rendering all items on every new insertion. On step k, appending one item causes k rendering DOM operations. Over N steps, the total operations accumulate to N*(N+1)/2, demonstrating an O(N^2) total quadratic runtime and an amortized O(N) cost per roll step.

pacman_a_star_lesson_a_star.name: Pacman-A-Star-Lesson — A* Search with Manhattan Distance Heuristic
pacman_a_star_lesson_a_star.rules: This function executes a deterministic A* search on a grid layout where walls are '1' and walkable tiles are '0', '2', or '3'. Using a priority queue ordered by total estimated cost f(n) = g(n) + h(n), tied by heuristic h(n) and insertion order, it iteratively expands the most promising cell. The heuristic h(n) is computed using Manhattan distance to the target coordinates. Upon reaching the goal cell, the algorithm reconstructs the shortest path, computes total animation duration based on 260ms per hop, and derives a padded bounding box around all visited cells.

pacman_a_star_heuristic_evaluation.name: Pacman-A-Star — A* Search Path Admissibility and Heuristic Evaluation
pacman_a_star_heuristic_evaluation.rules: This function deterministically traces the evaluation steps of A* search on a grid graph for Pacman. At each step, the algorithm pops the node with the lowest f-score f(n) = g(n) + h(n) from the priority queue, where g(n) is the exact path cost from start and h(n) is the admissible Manhattan distance heuristic to the goal. It records each node expansion as a checkpoint step until reaching the goal coordinates.

bouncer_id_check.name: Bouncer -- ID Check
bouncer_id_check.rules: Check each ID. Reject anyone underage, expired, or already let in tonight -- otherwise, let them in. This is the same admissible-threshold logic as binary search, wearing a doorman costume.
